subject: history
title: Nicholas II to October 1917
welcome_lead: From Tsarist autocracy to Bolshevik power.
meta_desc: A-Level Russia 1894-1941 adventure on Nicholas II, 1905, WWI and the 1917 Revolutions.
final_note: You can chart the collapse of Tsarism and the Bolshevik seizure of power.

concepts.def: Tsar 1894-1917, committed to autocracy; abdicated 15 March 1917 NS amid Petrograd unrest.
Massacre of unarmed petitioners outside the Winter Palace on 22 January 1905, sparking the 1905 Revolution.
Nicholas II's concession of civil liberties and an elected Duma, splitting the opposition.
Russia's costly war 1914-17: defeats at Tannenberg (1914) and Masurian Lakes contributed to regime collapse.
Petrograd uprising forcing Nicholas II's abdication on 15 March 1917 NS and creating Dual Power.
Bolshevik seizure of power on 25 October (OS) / 7 November (NS) 1917, organised by Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee.

walkthroughs.body_html: Industrialisation under Witte produced an urban working class and political parties: SDs (1898, split 1903), SRs (1901), Kadets (1905). The Russo-Japanese War (1904-05) and Bloody Sunday precipitated the 1905 Revolution. The October Manifesto and Fundamental Laws (April 1906) preserved autocratic prerogatives. Stolypin's agrarian reforms (1906-11) sought a 'wager on the strong'.

By 1917 Russian losses approached 1.7 million dead. Nicholas's assumption of command (September 1915) tied him to defeats. Rasputin's influence at court (until his murder, 30 December 1916) discredited the dynasty. Bread queues and the women's day strikes (8 March 1917) ignited the February Revolution; the Duma's Provisional Committee and the Petrograd Soviet emerged in tandem.

Lenin's April Theses rejected cooperation with the Provisional Government. The June Offensive failed; the July Days saw Lenin flee to Finland; the Kornilov Affair (August) discredited Kerensky. Bolshevik majorities in the Petrograd and Moscow Soviets enabled the October Revolution. The Second Congress of Soviets passed the Decrees on Peace and Land.
